projects.name: NBTMap Explorer
projects.description: Desktop application developed in C# to explore, visualize and export Minecraft item maps (map_*.dat) from NBT files, without needing to run Minecraft or use mods.

context.problem: Minecraft item maps are stored in NBT files that are not easily readable or viewable outside the game, making their analysis or reuse difficult.
context.role: Lead developer responsible for application logic, NBT parsing, map rendering and overall architecture. The UI prototype was designed in collaboration with a designer.
context.approach: Design and implementation of a desktop application in WPF following the MVVM pattern to read and process NBT data, interpret map information and export them as images.
challenges: Correctly understanding and parsing the NBT data structure
Rendering maps respecting scaling and colors
Detecting Minecraft installations and world paths in Windows
learnings: Working with binary formats and data structures
Practical application of the MVVM pattern in WPF
Separation of responsibilities between UI and business logic

projects.name: Pony the Dragon! [REP+]
projects.description: Complete mod for The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth (Repentance+) that introduces a new playable character with original items, mechanics and compatibility with other mods.

context.problem: Creating a fully functional and coherent character within The Binding of Isaac mod ecosystem, maintaining compatibility, balance and code quality.
context.role: Code cleanup, testing support and project maintenance.
context.approach: Mod developed in Lua using the game's official API, following engine conventions and ensuring compatibility with other popular mods.
challenges: Understanding and working on an existing codebase
learnings: Testing and debugging in non-traditional environments

projects.name: Monte Carlo Global Illumination Demo
projects.description: Academic demo exploring the use of the Monte Carlo method to approximate global illumination in a 3D environment.

context.problem: Demonstrate practical applications of the Monte Carlo method beyond classic examples like PI calculation, orienting it towards computer graphics.
context.role: Research, design and complete implementation of the project as university work.
context.approach: Implementation of a 3D environment using Python and OpenGL, with shaders written in GLSL and support from libraries like NumPy and pygame for mathematical handling and the rendering window.
challenges: Configuration and stability of the execution environment
Time limitations of the academic project
learnings: Recognition of academic scope limitations in technical projects
